newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-WEEKEND PROGRAMME IN THE GERMAN LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND PROGRAMME IN THE GERMAN LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: The following Bundesliga matches are scheduled to take place this weekend in addition to Sunday's top clash involving Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund.

Bochum are unbeaten at home this season winning four of their five games so far but must rearrange their defence. Thomas Stickroth absent because of suspension and former East German Torsten Kracht returns in his place after suspension. 1860 look like they want to attack, fielding two strikers.

Bayer Leverkusen (3) v VfB Stuttgart (1). One of two top-of-the-table clashes. Bayer coach Christoph Daum takes on the club which he led to the championship in 1992. Leverkusen welcome back former German international striker Ulf Kirsten after suspension. VfB must wait to see if Croat midfielder Zvonimir Soldo and defender Thomas Schneider recover from injuries.

Not quite a relegation battle at this stage of the season but these two teams are struggling. St Pauli have won just one of five games at home. The Hamburg club welcome back Andre Trulsen after suspension to lead the defence. Freiburg have injury worries about goalkeeper Joerg Schmadtke, Croat defender Damir Buric and midfielder Oliver Freund.

Borussia Moenchengladbach (11) v Hansa Rostock (14). Moenchengladbach need to bounce back after 4-2 home defeat in midweek by Monaco in UEFA Cup second round first leg. Rostock have quite good record away from home.

Karlsruhe riding crest of wave after impressive 3-0 defeat of Roma in UEFA Cup and plan to field unchanged team. Bremen have struggled away from home winning just one out of five matches. The northerners may be without German internationals Jens Todt (ankle) and Marco Bode (groin).

Schalke struggled to 1-0 home win over Turkey's Trabzonspor in UEFA Cup. Dutch forward Youri Mulder is suspended. Hamburg, fresh from impressive 3-0 destruction of Spartak Moscow in UEFA Cup, will be missing injured midfielder Harald Spoerl.

Newly-promoted Bielefeld have won just once this season and will be without injured midfielder Rob Maas. If defender Michael Kostner and midfielder Ralf Hauptmann are fit, Cologne can field first-choice line-up.

Duisburg have bounced back to form but face Fortuna team who have three away wins to their name so far. Duesseldorf may field Russian international midfielder Igor Dobrovolsky who joined on loan from Dynamo Moscow during week.
